description: The MATLAB unit testing framework (class-based and function-based tests, qualifications, fixtures, runners and coverage), performance measurement with the perftest framework and timeit, and static code analysis.

tools.name: matlab.unittest.TestCase
tools.description: The base class for class-based unit tests, where each method in a Test block is an individual test case. Setup and teardown methods run before and after each test or the whole class, and qualification methods (verify, assert, assume, fatalAssert) record failures. Class-based tests are the most capable style, supporting parameterization, fixtures and shared test data.
tools.usage:
classdef MyTest < matlab.unittest.TestCase
    properties (TestParameter)
        n = {1, 10, 100};
    end
    methods (TestMethodSetup)
        function setup(testCase); end
    end
    methods (Test)
        function tCase(testCase, n); end
    end
end

parameters.name: methods (Test)
parameters.description: Block whose methods are the individual test cases.

parameters.name: methods (TestMethodSetup/TestMethodTeardown)
parameters.description: Run before and after every test method.

parameters.name: methods (TestClassSetup/TestClassTeardown)
parameters.description: Run once for the whole class.

parameters.name: properties (TestParameter)
parameters.description: Cell or struct of values; tests run once per combination.

parameters.name: properties (TestTags)
parameters.description: Attribute used to tag tests for selective running.

tools.notes: verify records a failure and continues; assert stops the current test; fatalAssert aborts the whole run.

tools.name: runtests
tools.description: Discover and run tests from a file, folder, package or namespace and return an array of TestResult objects. Name/value options select tests by tag, name or procedure and enable parallel execution and code coverage. It is the standard one-line way to run a test suite.
tools.usage:
results = runtests
results = runtests(tests)
results = runtests(tests, Name, Value)
table(results)

parameters.name: tests
parameters.description: File name, folder, 'package.Name' or a cell array of them; defaults to the current folder.

parameters.name: 'IncludeSubfolders'
parameters.description: Logical; recurse into subfolders.

parameters.name: 'Tag'
parameters.description: Run only tests carrying the given tag.

parameters.name: 'Name'
parameters.description: Wildcard filter on the fully qualified test name.

parameters.name: 'UseParallel'
parameters.description: Logical; distribute the suite across a parallel pool.

parameters.name: 'OutputDetail' / 'LoggingLevel'
parameters.description: Verbosity of the console report.

parameters.name: 'ReportCoverageFor'
parameters.description: Files or folders for which to collect code coverage.

tools.notes: In CI, call assertSuccess(results) or exit(any([results.Failed])) so a failing suite fails the build.

tools.name: testsuite
tools.description: Build a suite of Test objects from files, folders or packages without running them, so the suite can be filtered, reordered, combined and handed to a customized TestRunner. Selection options let you pick tests by tag, name, superclass or parameter. It is the first step of any non-trivial test workflow.
tools.usage:
suite = testsuite
suite = testsuite(tests)
suite = testsuite(tests, Name, Value)
suite = selectIf(suite, constraint)
results = run(suite)

parameters.name: tests
parameters.description: File, folder, package name, or a cell array of them.

parameters.name: 'IncludeSubfolders' / 'IncludeSubpackages'
parameters.description: Recursive discovery options.

parameters.name: 'Tag'
parameters.description: Keep only tests with the given tag.

parameters.name: 'Name'
parameters.description: Wildcard filter on test names.

parameters.name: 'ParameterName' / 'ParameterProperty'
parameters.description: Select specific parameterizations.

parameters.name: 'BaseFolder'
parameters.description: Restrict to tests defined under a folder.

tools.name: matlab.unittest.TestRunner
tools.description: Runs a test suite with a configurable set of plugins that control reporting, code coverage, diagnostics, TAP or JUnit XML output and failure handling. Building a runner yourself is how you integrate MATLAB tests with a continuous integration system. The default runners cover the common console and silent cases.
tools.usage:
runner = testrunner('textoutput')
runner = matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withTextOutput
runner = matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withNoPlugins
addPlugin(runner, plugin)
results = run(runner, suite)

parameters.name: withTextOutput
parameters.description: Standard console-reporting runner; accepts an 'OutputDetail' level.

parameters.name: withNoPlugins
parameters.description: Bare runner to which you add exactly the plugins you want.

parameters.name: addPlugin
parameters.description: Attach a plugin such as CodeCoveragePlugin, TAPPlugin, XMLPlugin or FailureDiagnosticsPlugin.

tools.name: verifyEqual
tools.description: Qualify that an actual value equals an expected one, with optional absolute and relative tolerances for floating-point comparison. A failure is recorded and the test continues, which lets a single test report several problems. Class and size must match exactly unless you relax them with a constraint.
tools.usage:
verifyEqual(testCase, actual, expected)
verifyEqual(testCase, actual, expected, 'AbsTol', tol)
verifyEqual(testCase, actual, expected, 'RelTol', tol)
verifyEqual(___, diagnostic)

parameters.name: actual, expected
parameters.description: Values to compare; class, size and content must all match.

parameters.name: 'AbsTol'
parameters.description: Absolute tolerance for numeric comparison.

parameters.name: 'RelTol'
parameters.description: Relative tolerance, better for values spanning several magnitudes.

parameters.name: diagnostic
parameters.description: String or Diagnostic object shown when the qualification fails.

tools.notes: Comparing doubles without a tolerance almost always fails; always pass AbsTol or RelTol for floating-point results.

tools.name: verifyError
tools.description: Qualify that a function handle throws an error with a specific identifier or of a specific exception class. Testing failure paths is as important as testing success paths, especially for input validation. The function is called with no output arguments unless you request them.
tools.usage:
verifyError(testCase, actual, identifier)
verifyError(testCase, actual, metaClass)
verifyError(___, diagnostic)
[output1, ...] = verifyError(___)

parameters.name: actual
parameters.description: Function handle expected to throw, taking no arguments.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: Expected error identifier such as 'MATLAB:badsubscript'.

parameters.name: metaClass
parameters.description: ?MException subclass the thrown exception must belong to.

parameters.name: diagnostic
parameters.description: Message shown on failure.

tools.notes: verifyWarning, verifyWarningFree and verifyThat with the Throws constraint cover related cases.

tools.name: verifyTrue
tools.description: Qualify that a value is a scalar logical true. It is the simplest qualification, though verifyEqual, verifyGreaterThan and the constraint-based verifyThat usually give much clearer failure diagnostics. Anything other than a scalar logical true fails, including 1 of class double.
tools.usage:
verifyTrue(testCase, actual)
verifyTrue(testCase, actual, diagnostic)

parameters.name: actual
parameters.description: Value that must be a scalar logical true.

parameters.name: diagnostic
parameters.description: Message shown on failure; strongly recommended here.

tools.notes: verifyTrue(x == y) gives a poor failure message; prefer verifyEqual(x, y), which shows both values.

tools.name: assertEqual
tools.description: Assert that a value equals an expected one, aborting the current test method immediately if it does not. Use assertions for preconditions whose failure would make the rest of the test meaningless or produce cascading errors. Everything else should use the verify family so a single run reports all problems.
tools.usage:
assertEqual(testCase, actual, expected)
assertEqual(testCase, actual, expected, 'AbsTol', tol)
assertEqual(___, diagnostic)

parameters.name: actual, expected
parameters.description: Values that must match in class, size and content.

parameters.name: 'AbsTol' / 'RelTol'
parameters.description: Numeric comparison tolerances.

parameters.name: diagnostic
parameters.description: Message shown when the assertion fails.

tools.notes: assumeEqual marks the test filtered rather than failed, which is right for environment-dependent preconditions.

tools.name: verifyThat
tools.description: Qualify that a value satisfies a constraint object, which is the most expressive and best-diagnosing form of qualification. Dozens of constraints cover numeric tolerance, string matching, set membership, structural comparison and error throwing, and they combine with the & and | operators. Use it whenever a plain verifyEqual cannot express the requirement.
tools.usage:
verifyThat(testCase, actual, constraint)
verifyThat(testCase, actual, constraint, diagnostic)

parameters.name: constraint
parameters.description: A constraint from matlab.unittest.constraints such as IsEqualTo, IsGreaterThan, HasSize, ContainsSubstring, IsOfClass, Throws, IssuesWarnings.

parameters.name: diagnostic
parameters.description: Additional message shown on failure.

tools.name: functiontests
tools.description: Create a test suite from the local functions of a script-style test file, which is the function-based testing style. Local functions whose names start or end with 'test' become test cases, and setup/teardown functions provide fixtures. It is the lightest-weight way to write tests, at the cost of parameterization support.
tools.usage:
tests = functiontests(localfunctions)
tests = functiontests(fcnHandles)
% in the test file:
function tests = myFileTest
    tests = functiontests(localfunctions);
end

parameters.name: localfunctions
parameters.description: Cell array of handles to the file's local functions; call localfunctions with no arguments.

parameters.name: setupOnce / teardownOnce
parameters.description: Local functions run once for the whole file.

parameters.name: setup / teardown
parameters.description: Local functions run before and after each test.

parameters.name: testCase.TestData
parameters.description: Struct used to pass data from setup functions to the tests.

tools.name: matlab.unittest.fixtures.TemporaryFolderFixture
tools.description: A fixture that creates a temporary folder for a test and deletes it, with all its contents, when the test finishes. It guarantees that tests writing files leave no residue and cannot interfere with one another. Apply it with applyFixture inside a setup method or a test.

parameters.name: 'PreservingOnFailure'
parameters.description: Logical; keep the folder when the test fails so you can inspect its contents.

parameters.name: 'WithSuffix'
parameters.description: Suffix appended to the generated folder name.

parameters.name: f.Folder
parameters.description: Path of the created temporary folder.

tools.notes: CurrentFolderFixture, PathFixture, SuppressedWarningsFixture and WorkingFolderFixture cover the other common cases.

tools.name: matlab.unittest.plugins.CodeCoveragePlugin
tools.description: A test runner plugin that measures which lines, statements, decisions or conditions of your source code the test suite exercises. Reports can be produced as an interactive HTML page or as Cobertura XML for a CI server. Coverage highlights untested branches, which are where bugs hide.
tools.usage:
import matlab.unittest.plugins.CodeCoveragePlugin
plugin = CodeCoveragePlugin.forFolder(folder)
plugin = CodeCoveragePlugin.forFile(file, 'Producing', format)
plugin = CodeCoveragePlugin.forPackage(pkg)
addPlugin(runner, plugin)

parameters.name: forFolder / forFile / forPackage
parameters.description: What source code to instrument.

parameters.name: 'IncludingSubfolders'
parameters.description: Logical; recurse when using forFolder.

parameters.name: 'Producing'
parameters.description: A report format: CoverageReport (HTML), CoberturaFormat, or CoverageResult.

parameters.name: 'MetricLevel'
parameters.description: 'statement' (default), 'decision', 'condition' or 'mcdc'.

tools.name: runperf
tools.description: Run a test suite as a performance experiment, repeating each test until the measurements reach a target relative margin of error. It returns MeasurementResult objects with sample statistics rather than pass/fail outcomes. Use it to track execution time over time and to catch performance regressions.
tools.usage:
results = runperf
results = runperf(tests)
results = runperf(tests, Name, Value)
sampleSummary(results)

parameters.name: tests
parameters.description: File, folder or package containing the tests to measure.

parameters.name: 'IncludeSubfolders' / 'Tag' / 'Name'
parameters.description: Suite selection options, as for runtests.

parameters.name: 'RunIdentifier'
parameters.description: Label attached to the measurement results.

parameters.name: results(k).Samples
parameters.description: Table of individual timing measurements.

tools.notes: Write performance tests as a matlab.perftest.TestCase subclass and use startMeasuring/stopMeasuring to time only the region of interest.

tools.name: matlab.perftest.TimeExperiment
tools.description: Configure how a performance experiment is run: fixed sample counts for quick comparisons, or variable sampling that keeps measuring until a statistical target is met. Warm-up runs remove JIT and first-call overhead from the measurements. It gives far more control than the plain runperf entry point.
tools.usage:
import matlab.perftest.TimeExperiment
exp = TimeExperiment.limitingSamplingError
exp = TimeExperiment.limitingSamplingError(Name, Value)
exp = TimeExperiment.withFixedSampleSize(n)
results = run(exp, suite)

parameters.name: limitingSamplingError
parameters.description: Keep sampling until the relative margin of error target is met.

parameters.name: withFixedSampleSize
parameters.description: Take exactly n measurements per test.

parameters.name: 'NumWarmups'
parameters.description: Untimed warm-up runs before measurement begins.

parameters.name: 'RelativeMarginOfError'
parameters.description: Target precision, default 0.05 (5%).

parameters.name: 'MaxSamples' / 'MinSamples'
parameters.description: Bounds on the number of measurements.

parameters.name: 'ConfidenceLevel'
parameters.description: Confidence level for the margin of error, default 0.95.

tools.name: timeit
tools.description: Measure how long a function takes to run, automatically choosing a repetition count and returning a robust median time. It is far more reliable than tic/toc for short operations because it excludes first-call overhead and averages out noise. The function handle must take no input arguments, so close over the data.
tools.usage:
t = timeit(f)
t = timeit(f, numOutputs)

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function handle with no input arguments; capture data in a closure.

parameters.name: numOutputs
parameters.description: Number of outputs the function should produce, which can change how much work it does.

tools.notes: gputimeit is the GPU equivalent, which accounts for asynchronous kernel execution.

tools.name: profile
tools.description: Start, stop and view the MATLAB code profiler, which records how much time is spent in each function and on each line. The generated report ranks functions by self time and highlights the hottest lines, which is where optimization effort belongs. Always profile before optimizing rather than guessing.
tools.usage:
profile on
profile off
profile viewer
p = profile('info')
profile('on', '-history')
profile clear
profsave(p, folder)

parameters.name: 'on' / 'off' / 'resume' / 'clear'
parameters.description: Control the profiler state.

parameters.name: 'viewer'
parameters.description: Stop profiling and open the interactive HTML report.

parameters.name: 'info'
parameters.description: Return the profile data as a structure for programmatic analysis.

parameters.name: '-history'
parameters.description: Also record the sequence of function calls.

parameters.name: '-timer'
parameters.description: 'performance' (default), 'cpu', 'real' or 'processor'.

tools.notes: Profiling adds overhead, so use the reported proportions rather than the absolute times.

tools.name: checkcode
tools.description: Run the MATLAB Code Analyzer statically over a file, reporting possible errors, unused variables, inefficient patterns and style problems. With output arguments it returns a structure array you can assert on in a test, which enforces code quality in CI. Message IDs let you suppress specific checks deliberately.
tools.usage:
checkcode(filename)
info = checkcode(filename)
info = checkcode(filename, '-id')
checkcode(filename, '-config=factory')
info = checkcode(filename, '-cyc')

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: One or more .m file names.

parameters.name: '-id'
parameters.description: Include the message identifier of each finding.

parameters.name: '-cyc'
parameters.description: Also report McCabe cyclomatic complexity per function.

parameters.name: '-config=factory'
parameters.description: Use the factory default settings instead of user preferences.

parameters.name: '-fullpath'
parameters.description: Treat the argument as a full path rather than a function name.

tools.notes: codeIssues (R2023a and later) returns a table and is the preferred programmatic interface in newer releases.

tools.name: validateattributes
tools.description: Validate that an input has the required class, size and value attributes, throwing a clear, standardized error if it does not. It replaces long chains of hand-written if/error checks with one declarative call. Supplying the function name and argument position makes the error message much easier to act on.
tools.usage:
validateattributes(A, classes, attributes)
validateattributes(A, classes, attributes, funcName)
validateattributes(A, classes, attributes, funcName, varName, argIndex)

parameters.name: classes
parameters.description: Cell array of allowed classes, e.g. {'numeric'}, {'double','single'}, {'char','string'}.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Cell array such as {'nonempty','positive','integer','scalar','vector','2d','real','finite','nonnan','increasing','>=', 0, '<=', 1, 'size', [3 NaN]}.

parameters.name: funcName, varName, argIndex
parameters.description: Context used to build a readable error message.

tools.notes: In new code, an arguments block gives the same validation declaratively and also supports defaults and name-value arguments.

tools.name: assert
tools.description: Throw an error when a condition is false, optionally with a formatted message and an error identifier. Use it for internal invariants and preconditions in production code, separate from the test framework's assertion methods. The identifier lets callers catch and handle specific failures.
tools.usage:
assert(cond)
assert(cond, msg)
assert(cond, msg, A1, ..., An)
assert(cond, errID, msg, A1, ..., An)

parameters.name: cond
parameters.description: Condition that must be true; must be a scalar logical or convertible to one.

parameters.name: errID
parameters.description: Error identifier of the form 'component:mnemonic'.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Message text, optionally with printf-style format specifiers.

tools.notes: Use assert for programmer errors and error() for expected runtime conditions such as a missing file.

tools.name: arguments
tools.description: Declare a function's input and output argument types, sizes, default values and validation functions in a block at the top of the function. It replaces nargin checks, inputParser and hand-written validation with a concise, self-documenting declaration that also drives tab completion. Name-value arguments are declared with a nested structure or the Repeating attribute.
tools.usage:
function out = myFcn(x, opts)
    arguments
        x (1,:) double {mustBeFinite}
        opts.Method (1,1) string {mustBeMember(opts.Method, ["fast","accurate"])} = "fast"
        opts.Tolerance (1,1) double {mustBePositive} = 1e-6
    end
end

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Dimension specification such as (1,1), (1,:), (:,3); values are validated and scalar-expanded.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Required class; compatible inputs are converted automatically.

parameters.name: {validators}
parameters.description: mustBePositive, mustBeFinite, mustBeMember, mustBeNumeric, mustBeText, mustBeInRange, or your own function.

parameters.name: = default
parameters.description: Default value, which makes the argument optional.

parameters.name: arguments (Output)
parameters.description: Block validating the function's outputs.

tools.notes: The arguments block must be the very first code in the function, before any executable statement.
